transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because I haven’t really been myself lately. I keep losing my temper over small things—snapping on operations calls, getting short with people at home. I don’t mean to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s not how I usually handle things, and it’s starting to bother me.
Have you been having any recurring thoughts or urges that you can't seem to get out of your head?

Yeah… a bit. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it does happen. I’ll be sitting at the kitchen table, or trying to answer emails from home, and out of nowhere I’m seeing that flash from the valve again, and the smoke in the aisle. It’s like it pushes everything else out of my head for a minute. I don’t know if that’s what you mean.
Have you been avoiding certain places, people, or activities since these flashes started happening?

I’m not sure I’d call it avoiding, exactly. I mean… I still do what I need to do. I haven’t really noticed myself staying away from specific people or places on purpose. Maybe I’m a little more careful about what I get into, but I don’t know if that counts. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about everyday things, even when there's no apparent reason to worry?

I don’t think so… not in the usual way, anyway. I mean, everybody worries about work and bills and family stuff, right? But I wouldn’t say I’m sitting around worrying for no reason all the time. At least, I haven’t really noticed that being the main issue. Is that what you’re asking?
Have you been having trouble sleeping lately?

Yeah… sleep’s been pretty rough, I guess. I try not to make too much of it, but most nights I just lie there and it’s like I can still hear that alarm in my head. Then if I do finally fall asleep, I’ll wake up sweating from dreams about the smoke and people yelling. By morning I feel like I didn’t really sleep at all. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been experiencing any physical symptoms like headaches or tremors?

I don’t think so, no… at least nothing I’d call serious. I mean, I get normal aches and stuff like anyone, but I haven’t noticed headaches or shaking in a way that stands out. If there’s something specific I should be watching for, I can try to pay more attention.
Do you find yourself constantly on the lookout for potential dangers or threats?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m paranoid or anything, but I do catch myself doing that. Like if I hear a forklift beep, or a compressor kick on, or even just the smoke alarm chirping at home, my whole body kind of locks up. I start looking around for exits, checking what could go wrong next… probably more than I need to. Is that what you mean?
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body, watching yourself?

Um… I don’t think so. Not like I’m watching myself from across the room or anything. Sometimes I feel kind of spaced out, I guess, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean. I’m trying to answer right—I just haven’t really noticed that specific feeling.
Do you ever feel numb or disconnected from your feelings or surroundings?

Yeah… maybe a little. I mean, I’m still there, I’m not totally checked out or anything. But my wife will make dinner, or the kids are talking about soccer like everything’s normal, and I know I should feel happy to be sitting there with them. I want to. But it’s like… there’s nothing in me that really responds. I don’t know if that’s what you mean by numb.
Are there any specific activities or situations that you've been trying to avoid because they remind you of what happened?

I’m not sure… I mean, nothing I’d call deliberate, I guess. I haven’t sat down and made a list of things I won’t do. Maybe I steer around certain stuff without really thinking about it, but I don’t want to overstate it. What kinds of activities do you mean?
Do you often feel guilty about what happened?

I… I don’t know. I don’t want to say yes if that makes it sound like I’m blaming myself for the whole thing or something. I guess I’ve had moments where I think, “Could I have done something different?” but I don’t know if that’s guilt exactly. Maybe that’s normal?
Do you experience memories of the incident that feel like they're happening all over again, as if you're reliving them?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it happens. I can be sitting at the kitchen table, or trying to answer emails from home, and then all of a sudden I’m right back there—seeing the flash from that valve and the smoke in the aisle. It’s like it shoves everything else out of my head for a minute. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Has your behavior or these experiences been causing problems for you at work or in your relationships with family and friends?

Yeah… it’s causing problems, more than I’d like to admit. I haven’t even been cleared to go back to the plant yet, so that’s already an issue. And I’m trying to keep up from home, but on calls I’ll miss things or lose the thread, and then people get frustrated.

I don’t want to make excuses—I know they need me to be steady—but I can tell I’ve upset some folks. I’m starting to worry I’m becoming more of a liability than the manager they need right now, if that makes sense.
Are there specific places or situations that remind you of the incident with the valve and smoke, which you now try to avoid?

I’m not sure I can point to specific places, honestly. I mean… I don’t think I’m, like, making a list of places I can’t go or anything.

There are moments where something sort of reminds me of it, but I don’t know if I’m avoiding it on purpose or just… not wanting to deal with it right then. Does that make sense? I don’t want to overstate it.
How long have you been experiencing these flashes and trouble sleeping?

It’s been… about three weeks, I guess. Since the valve failed and that injury happened at the facility. I kept thinking it would settle down after a few days, so I didn’t want to make too much of it, but it’s pretty much been going on since then.
Have you avoided returning to the plant where the incident occurred?

I… I haven’t really gone back, no. But I’m not sure I’d call it avoiding exactly. I mean, I haven’t been cleared to return yet, so part of it is just that.

If I’m being honest, I haven’t pushed very hard to get back in there either. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean. I’d like to think I’m just following the process, but… yeah, maybe there’s a part of me that’s not eager to walk back into that place right now.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

I wouldn’t say I’ve stopped caring about everything, exactly. I still… you know, I try to be there.

But it’s different. My wife will make dinner, or my kids will be talking about soccer like they always do, and I know I should feel happy just being with them. I want to feel that. It’s just… sometimes it’s like there’s nothing in me that responds. Like I’m sitting there doing the right thing, but I’m not really feeling it.

I don’t know if that counts as losing interest, but it doesn’t feel normal for me.
Have you felt like you're unable to fulfill your responsibilities at work or at home because of these experiences?

I’m trying to keep up, I really am. I haven’t been cleared to go back to the plant yet, so that part is kind of out of my hands.

But even working from home… I’m missing things on calls. People will ask me something and I realize I didn’t catch half of what was said, or I forget to follow up on something I normally wouldn’t miss. I’ve upset a couple people because of it.

I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t do my job, but… honestly, I’m worried I’m becoming more of a liability than the manager they need right now. At home I’m still trying, but work especially has been hard.
